CVE-2026-120720.title: S3 bucket name controls the request host in ex_aws virtual-host requests
CVE-2026-120720.description:
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 bucket name to send the application's signed S3 requests to a host of their choice.

With virtual_host: true, ExAws.Operation.S3.add_bucket_to_path/2 in lib/ex_aws/operation/s3.ex builds the request hostname from the bucket name and the configured host without checking the bucket name. A bucket such as attacker.example/x? turns the request URL into https://attacker.example/x?.s3.amazonaws.com/key, so the request is signed for and sent to attacker.example. The attacker receives upload bodies, the access key id and request signature, and any STS session token, and controls the response the application parses. With bucket_as_host: true the bucket is the whole hostname, so any valid hostname redirects the request.

This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.7 before 2.8.0.

CVE-2026-120755.title: Integer Underflow Leads to Out-of-Bounds Read via Truncated Chunk in HDF5 Szip Filter
CVE-2026-120755.description: HDF5 through 2.2.0 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in H5Z__filter_szip() in src/H5Zszip.c. When decoding a szip-compressed chunk, the function subtracts the 4-byte uncompressed-length header from the chunk length without first verifying that the chunk is at least 4 bytes long. A truncated or corrupted chunk shorter than the header causes the length calculation to wrap around to a very large value, and the decompressor reads far past the end of the chunk buffer. An attacker who can get a user or application to read a dataset from a crafted HDF5 file can cause a denial of service. Only builds with szip support (libaec or the szip library) are affected.

CVE-2026-99321.title: rust_binder: wake epoll on self-work queued to poll thread
CVE-2026-99321.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

rust_binder: wake epoll on self-work queued to poll thread

When a thread pushes work to its own todo list, InnerThread::push_work()
returns PushWorkRes::OkNotifyPoll if the thread uses epoll, but four
call sites in thread.rs discard this return value. As a result, a
non-blocking BC_* write that enqueues work onto the calling thread's
todo list without also reading will not wake epoll. Check the return
value and call self.process.notify_poll(false) when
PushWorkRes::OkNotifyPoll is returned.

This is similar to commit 97830f3c3088 ("binder: signal epoll threads of
self-work"), but in C Binder pending thread work also prevented
subsequent process work from waking epoll, causing a permanent hang,
which is not the case in Rust Binder. This means that in practice, it
merely delays notifications rather than completely failing to send them.
